overview: Global markets and corporate governance face turbulence following an investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged affair, causing the chip maker's shares to drop. In commercial real estate, U.S. office leasing rose in the third quarter as tenant footprints stabilized, while California voters rejected a measure that would have streamlined housing and development construction. San Francisco's local developments include the approval of the city's first-ever public bank measure and out-of-state investors targeting downtown office purchases. Meanwhile in Hawaii, Hawaiian Electric's parent company sustained profits despite financial hits from recent storms, and Maui families continue the arduous process of wildfire recovery three years later.

wiki.title: SoHo Weekly News
wiki.extract: The SoHo Weekly News (SWN) was a weekly alternative newspaper founded by American music publicist Michael Goldstein and published in New York City from 1973 to 1982. Goldstein positioned the paper as a competitor to The Village Voice, an established alternative newspaper, but it struggled financially. SWN was acquired by Associated Newspaper Group in 1979 and ceased publication three years later after the company was unable to make it profitable.
